Professional profile

Martin Stefanov.

I work in the Cyber Defense Section at DSK Bank in Sofia, where I investigate phishing, endpoint detections and web threats. Beyond incident response, I build software for analysts, research how language models handle sensitive data, and conduct penetration tests in web, API and Active Directory environments.

Professional experience

Oct 2021 – present

Cyber Defense Analyst (SOC)

DSK Bank
  • Reconstruct the timeline of an alert using SIEM, endpoint, proxy and web records. Compare timestamps and affected assets before deciding what to escalate.
  • Investigate suspicious messages, attachments and URLs. Email authentication, sender context and endpoint activity contribute different pieces of evidence to the case.
  • Review WAF and DDoS alerts with infrastructure and application teams. Establish whether a service was affected and document the evidence and next checks.
  • Write scripts for repeated lookups, evidence collection and reporting. Prepare case summaries and handovers for technical colleagues and users in Bulgarian and English.
Oct 2020 – Sep 2021

Network Administration & Support

Digital Systems
  • Monitored and supported network devices, servers and workstations, investigated connectivity problems and assisted users with service interruptions.
  • Helped deploy infrastructure and resolve configuration and hardware issues. The role gave me a practical basis for distinguishing a security event from a service fault.
Sep 2013 – Apr 2014

Technical Support Intern

Infotech / Sony VAIO Service
  • Diagnosed faults in laptops and desktops, assisted with repairs and explained the findings to customers. It was my starting point in hands-on troubleshooting.

Selected project work

Private project · analyst tooling

SOC Tool

I developed an analyst workspace that brings indicator checks and case evidence into one interface. The July web edition grew from earlier desktop utilities. Its project page shows the browser interface with demonstration data.

AI data protection

AI DLP Guard

I built browser extensions, a workstation agent and a policy console. In a documented local test I compared how the same policy handled prompt text and an image. Zero findings meant something different when the scanner could not read the input.

AI evaluation

LLM Red Team Lab

I built a workbench for reviewing model evaluations. It ties a finding to its transcript, keeps confidence separate from severity and lets me compare runs against a baseline.

Scientific software

Zero-G Firewall

I combined public NASA microgravity combustion data, a browser-based model and a 3D interface. The project’s validation note explains how holding out an experimental regime changes the question the model is answering.

How I work

I started in hardware repair and network support. The SOC taught me to follow the same event through several systems — an email can look convincing until the endpoint or identity evidence tells a different story. That practical question of what evidence an analyst needs drives most of my engineering work.

Incident investigation

I work from the original alert to a timeline. I compare email authentication results and message content with endpoint, identity and network events, then record which evidence supports the assessment and what the next analyst should check.

AI security and red-team research

In my lab I compare how applications behave when the prompt, retrieved documents or tool permissions change. I keep the conversation and configuration alongside each finding so a second reviewer can judge it.

Penetration testing

In web, API and Active Directory labs I practise scoped assessments, grading findings and writing reproducible reports. My CPTS work developed the habit of explaining the security consequence and proposing a fix an engineer can verify.

Security software and automation

I use Python, PowerShell, JavaScript and REST APIs to connect analyst tools. I pay attention to batch processing, timeouts, partial responses and the evidence that survives a CSV export or shift handover.

Wireless systems

My engineering physics background and Class 2 amateur radio licence inform my wireless research. My master’s work examined the command link and camera stream of a Ryze Tello. The results became a co-authored conference paper.

MSc · Protection of Information in Computer Systems and Networks

2020

Technical University of Sofia

Studying measurement, signals and physical systems shaped my approach to security testing. I still start by asking what was actually measured and under which conditions.

Publication and team award

IEEE COMCONF · 2024

Analysis of Drone Security

Martin Stefanov, Milen Petrov and Adelina Aleksieva-Petrova.

In five laboratory tests we examined access to the Wi-Fi network, the reliability of the control link and camera privacy on a Ryze Tello. The work grew out of my master’s research.
